title: KY PSC Order — Case No. 2011-00450: ELECTRONIC INVESTIGATION OF THE RELIABILITY MEASURES OF KENTUCKY’S JURISDICTIONAL ELECTRIC DISTRIBUTION UTILITIES
text:
COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY 

BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 

In the Matter of: 

ELECTRONIC INVESTIGATION OF THE 
RELIABILITY MEASURES OF KENTUCKY’S 
JURISDICTIONAL ELECTRIC DISTRIBUTION 
UTILITIES 
) 
) 
) 
) 

CASE NO. 
2011-00450 
O R D E R 
Every year each electric utility files its Reliability Report and Vegetation 
Management Update in this matter.1 Duke Kentucky Energy, Inc. (Duke Kentucky) has 
filed petitions annually,2 pursuant to 807 KAR 5:001, Section 13, and KRS 61.878, 
requesting that the Commission grant confidential treatment for an indefinite period for 
the physical addresses of its substations and circuits.3 
In support of its petitions, Duke Kentucky argued that the information, if openly 
disclosed, could present security and safety issues by identifying locations of critical utility 
infrastructure that would unnecessarily expose the public to potential harm if exploited.4 

1 Order (Ky. PSC May 30, 2013). 
2 This Order will address the petition filed each year from 2023 through 2026. 
3 Duke Kentucky’s Petition for Confidential Treatment (Apr. 2026 Petition) (filed Apr. 28, 2026); 
Duke Kentucky’s Petition for Confidential Treatment (May 2025 Petition) (filed May 1, 2025); Duke 
Kentucky’s Petition for Confidential Treatment (May 2024 Petition) (filed May 1, 2024); Duke Kentucky’s 
Petition for Confidential Treatment (May 2023 Petition) (May 1, 2023). The May 2023 Petition does not 
reference the correct confidentiality section of KRS 61.878. 
4 Apr. 2026 Petition at 2; May 2025 Petition at 2-3; May 2024 Petition at 2; May 2023 Petition at 2. 

-2- 
Case No. 2011-00450 
Duke Kentucky claimed that disclosure of this information could result in possible security 
issues such as including theft, destruction, possible injury, and vandalism.5 
Having considered the petitions and the material at issue, the Commission finds 
that disclosure of the physical addresses of utility infrastructure would result in 
compromising infrastructure security and as such is generally recognized as confidential; 
it therefore meets the criteria for confidential treatment and should be exempted from 
public disclosure pursuant to 807 KAR 5:001, Section 13, and KRS 61.878(1)(m). 
IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED that: 
1. 
Duke Kentucky’s April 28, 2026 petition for confidential treatment is granted. 
2. 
Duke Kentucky’s May 1, 2025 petition for confidential treatment is granted. 
3. 
Duke Kentucky’s May 1, 2024 petition for confidential treatment is granted. 
4. 
Duke Kentucky’s May 1, 2023 petition for confidential treatment is granted. 
5. 
The designated material granted confidential treatment by this Order shall 
not be placed in the public record or made available for public inspection for an indefinite 
period or until further order of this Commission. 
6. 
Use of the designated material granted confidential treatment by this Order 
in any Commission proceeding shall comply with 807 KAR 5:001, Section 13(9). 
7. 
If the designated material granted confidential treatment by this Order 
becomes publicly available or no longer qualifies for confidential treatment, Duke 
Kentucky shall inform the Commission and file with the Commission an unredacted copy 
of the designated material. 

5 Apr. 2026 Petition at 2; May 2025 Petition at 2-3; May 2024 Petition at 2; May 2023 Petition at 
2. 

-3- 
Case No. 2011-00450 
8. 
If a nonparty to this proceeding requests to inspect the material granted 
confidential treatment by this Order and the period during which the material has been 
granted confidential treatment has not expired, Duke Kentucky shall have 20 days from 
receipt of written notice of the request to demonstrate that the material still falls within the 
exclusions from disclosure requirements established in KRS 61.878. If Duke Kentucky is 
unable to make such demonstration, the requested material shall be made available for 
inspection. Otherwise, the Commission shall deny the request for inspection. 
9. 
The Commission shall not make the requested material available for 
inspection for 30 days from the date of service of an Order finding that the material no 
longer qualifies for confidential treatment in order to allow Duke Kentucky to seek a 
remedy afforded by law. 

Case No. 2011-00450 
Entered on this 6th day of July, 2026.
